assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Impact map states: 'Priority: Critical — inherited from Feature TC-9003, propagated to all created tasks'. The additional_fields section shows '"priority": {"name": "Critical"}'. Summary-comment.md confirms: 'Priority: Critical — propagated from Feature TC-9003 to all 10 created tasks. The Feature's priority is set (not "Undefined"), so it is inherited per the conditional inclusion rules.'

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Impact map states: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — inherited from Feature TC-9003, propagated to all created tasks (fixVersion scope defaults to "both" per Jira Field Defaults)'. The additional_fields section shows '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. Summary-comment.md confirms: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — propagated from Feature TC-9003 to all 10 created tasks. The Feature has a non-empty fixVersions array, and the fixVersion scope in Jira Field Defaults defaults to "both" (no explicit setting found), so fixVersions are propagated to tasks.'
